newsitem.title: GERMANY: Paribas downgrades Deutsche to 'no action'.
newsitem.headline: Paribas downgrades Deutsche to 'no action'.

text.p: Paribas said on Thursday it had downgraded its recommendation on Germany's Deutsche Bank AG to "no action" from "buy", having cut its earnings forecast for the stock for 1997.
In a statement, Paribas said it had cut its earnings per share forecast for Deutsche in 1997 by 12 percent to 4.4 marks.
It cited various factors for the downgrade, such as a 20 percent rise in operating expenses last year and the improbability of trading income matching its strong rise of 1996 in the current year.
"What is worse, costs for 1997 are to rise by seven percent at least, which lowers our forecasts by one billion marks straight away," Paribas said.
Paribas also noted that mismanagement at Deutsche's U.K. funds unit Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) cost Deutsche 1.2 billion, which had been hidden from view by gains on asset disposals.
Paribas's forecast for earnings per share in 1998 is 5.1 marks and six marks for 1999.
Deutsche detailed its 1996 results on Wednesday.
